title: Add langfuse instrumentation
description:
The following environment variables must be added to .env:

LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY
LANGFUSE_HOST

If these are not available, the app will still work, you just won't get any instrumentation.

See https://langfuse.com/integrations/model-providers/anthropic

title: tests(gh-actions): Add nightly & CI tests
description:
Add a smoke test that checks if shiny assistant is available and able to respond to user queries when 
- A team member creates a PR (Runs against the local version of shiny assistant)
- Nightly at 0300 hrs. (Runs against the deployed version of shiny assistant)

title: refactor: Remove reactive.lock() and reactive.flush() from the app
description:
**Merge this after py-shiny 1.9.0 is released.** It includes posit-dev/py-shiny#2549. On earlier py-shiny releases, the stream handler's reactive updates do not reach the client without `await reactive.flush()`.

py-shiny no longer has a global reactive lock (posit-dev/py-shiny#2549), and `reactive.lock()` is deprecated and returns a lock that does nothing (posit-dev/py-shiny#2520). Setting a reactive value now schedules a flush by itself. This PR removes the two uses in `shinyapp/app.py`.

## Changes

- **Stream handler (`transform_response`):** sets `shinylive_panel_visible` and `files_in_shinyapp_tags` directly, without the lock and without `await reactive.flush()`.
- **Done callback:** `sync_latest_messages_locked()` was only a wrapper that took the lock, so it is removed. The callback starts `sync_latest_messages()` directly. A [code comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/shiny-assistant/pull/15/files#diff-e839fa850483e449d3ca3396c4b2582602e0cd8c933ee6f334b8963cc9382d83) records why the task still sees the final message.

- **Requirements:** `shinyapp/requirements.txt` now requires `shiny>=1.9.0`.

## Why this is safe

- **No lost updates.** Without a flush after each `set()`, several sets can merge into one flush. That does not matter here: `shinylive_panel_visible` only changes from `False` to `True`, and `files_in_shinyapp_tags` is set once per response, to the full list of files. The effects use only the latest value.
- **No races on plain Python state.** In `sync_latest_messages()`, the code reads and updates `last_message_sent` with no `await` between them. Two concurrent calls therefore get different slices of the messages, and each one starts its send before it yields, so the client gets them in order. A local `asyncio.Lock` is not necessary.
- **The final message is stored before the sync task runs.** shinychat stores the message right after the transform function returns, before the stream task yields, so the task created in the done callback reads the complete message.

## Verification

I ran the app against py-shiny `main` with a fake Anthropic client that streams a reply with a `<SHINYAPP>` block, and sent three chat turns from Playwright. Each turn sent one `set-shinylive-content` message with the complete file, and synced the user message and the complete assistant message. The panel opened once. There were no errors and no `reactive.lock()` warnings.

## Not in this PR

To run the app for the check above, I had to work around two existing incompatibilities with current shinychat releases, which this PR does not fix: `chat.messages()` no longer takes `transform_user` or `transform_assistant`, and shinychat 0.7 requires `history=False` when `Chat` gets `messages=`.
